channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DECODED: THE AI CONVERSATIONS
channel.desc: AI is no longer a technology of the future; it is a current reality reshaping our daily lives and entire industries. Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.title: DIPLOMAT'S ARCHIVE: HIDDEN STORIES
channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

channel.desc: Es ist ein wahres Fest, das neue Jahr mit einem der besten Orchester der Welt zu begr??en! Die Gala aus Berlin von 2003 pr?sentiert die herausragenden Berliner Philharmoniker unter der Leitung von Sir Simon Rattle, mit Werken von Maurice Ravel ("Pavane pour une infante d?funte"; "La Valse"; Daphnis et Chlo?, Suite Nr. 2) und Werken von George Gershwin: "By Strauss", "How Long Has This Been Going On", "Nice Work If You Can Get It", "Embaceable You", "'S Wonderful" und "A Foggy Day". Mit ihrer reichen, ausdrucksstarken und nat?rlichen Stimme, ihrer rhythmischen Virtuosit?t und ihrer improvisatorischen Leichtigkeit ist sie unverkannbar f?rs Genre des Jazz geboren. Reeves wird von Peter Martin (Klavier), Rueben Rogers (Bass) und Greg Hutchinson (Schlagzeug) begleitet. Mit dabei: Peter Martin (Klavier) Rueben Rogers (Bass) Gregory Hutchinson (Schlagzeug).

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Fidelio (auch "Leonore, oder Der Triumph der ehelichen Liebe" genannt), Op. 72, ist Ludwig van Beethovens einzige Oper. Diese Opernverfilmung von 2018 aus dem schweizer Theater St. Gallen basiert auf der gefeierten B?hneninszenierung der Oper von Jan Schmidt-Garre. Dirigent Otto Tausk dirigiert das Sinfonieorchester und den Chor des St. Gallen-Theaters, sowie eine Reihe wunderbarer Solisten. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Tschaikowski ? Fantasie-Ouvert?re Romeo und Julia
channel.desc: Mozarts Violinkonzert Nr. 3 in G-Dur KV 216 Strawinskys "Fr?hlingsopfer" Jedes Jahr wird das Europakonzert von den Berliner Philharmonikern in einem bekannten saal oder an einem besonderen Ort veranstaltet. Das diesj?hrige wird in der pr?chtigen Royal Albert Hall in London aufgef?hrt. Der niederl?ndische Dirigent Bernard Haitink beginnt mit Tschaikowskys Fantasie-Ouvert?re aus "Romeo und Julia". W?hrend seiner Karriere spielte dieser mit vielen ber?hmten Orchestern und Dirigenten, wie dem Boston Symphony Orchestra und Mariss Jansons. Zimmermann hat eine gro?e Leidenschaft f?r Kammermusik und spielt viele Liederabende mit dem italienischen Pianisten Enrico Pace. Das schlie?t mit Strawinskys "Fr?hlingsopfer" ab, das der Komponist 1913 f?r Sergei Diaghilevs Ballets Russes schrieb. Das "Fr?hlingsopfer" gilt heute als eines der Meisterwerke der klassischen Musikgeschichte und hat viele Komponisten des 20. Jahrhunderts beeinflusst. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Verdi ? Messa da Requiem
channel.desc: Roberto Abbado dirigiert die Filarmonica Arturo Toscanini, den Coro del Teatro Regio di Parma und vier Gesangssolisten in einer herausragenden Auff?hrung von Giuseppe Verdis Messa da Requiem, aufgezeichnet im Parco Ducale di Parma in Italien w?hrend des Festival Verdi 2020. Die Solisten sind Sopranistin Eleonora Buratto, Mezzosopranistin Anita Rachvelishvili, Tenor Giorgio Berrugi und Bass Roberto Tagliavini. Als 1868 sein Komponistenkollege Gioachino Rossini starb, schlug Verdi vor, eine "Messa per Rossini" zu dessen Ehren zu komponieren, die von ihm selbst und mehreren anderen italienischen Komponisten geschrieben werden sollte. Verdi schrieb den abschlie?enden Satz, "Libera me". Als die Premiere abgesagt wurde, wurde das Projekt auf Eis gelegt. Als einige Jahre sp?ter der italienische Dichter Alessandro Manzoni verstarb, nahm Verdi seinen Plan wieder auf, ein Requiem zu komponieren ? diesmal zu Ehren des Dichters, den er so sehr bewunderte. Als Opernkomponist wusste Verdi besser als jeder andere, wie man das Werk dramatisch gestaltet, was in der ?berarbeiteten Version seines "Libera me" deutlich wird. Besonders herausragend ist das ber?hmte, kraftvolle "Dies Irae", das die Schrecken des J?ngsten Gerichts darstellt. Mit dabei: Eleonora Buratto (Sopran) Anita Rachvelishvili (Mezzosopran) Giorgio Berrugi (Tenor) Roberto Tagliavini (Bass).

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.name: Classica DE

In dieser Chaconne wird ein Thema vorgestellt, zu dem Bach eine Reihe kontinuierlicher Variationen entwickelt, die ein komplexes Spektrum harmonischer M?glichkeiten ausloten. Die Sonate Nr. 3 enth?lt eine umfangreiche Fuge, in der Bach viele kontrapunktische Techniken einsetzt. In dieser wunderbaren Auff?hrung zeigt Faust ihre Beherrschung der technisch anspruchsvollen St?cke Bachs. Dieses wurde 2020 in der Thomaskirche in Leipzig aufgezeichnet. channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Das renommierte franz?sische Streichquartett Quatuor ?b?ne feierte den 250. Geburtstag von Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) mit einem au?ergew?hnlichen Projekt: der Aufnahme aller sechzehn Streichquartette des gro?en Komponisten. F?nf Jahre lang tauchten die Geiger Pierre Colombet und Gabriel Le Magadure, die Bratschistin Marie Chilemme und der Cellist Rapha?l Merlin in Beethovens 650 Seiten umfassenden Partituren ein. Ihre Bem?hungen gipfelten in der Auff?hrung des gesamten Repertoires f?r Streichquartett, das drei Jahrzehnte von Beethovens musikalischer Kreativit?t umfasst, in sechs beeindruckenden en in der Philharmonie de Paris im Herbst 2020. Quatuor ?b?ne erforschte jede Facette von Beethovens Streichquartettrepertoire: von den fr?hen Streichquartetten Opus 18 bis zu den Razumovsky-, Harfen- und Serioso-Quartetten (Opus 59, 74 und 95) aus seiner mittleren Schaffensphase und schlie?lich die Tiefe seiner sp?ten Quartette (Opus 127 bis 135). channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Bach ? Sonate Nr. 2 BWV 1015
channel.desc: Johann Sebastian Bach probably wrote this set of six Sonatas for Violin and Harpsichord during his time as chapel master in K?then. channel.desc: Riccardo Chaillys Er?ffnungskonzert als Kapellmeister des Leipziger Gewandhausorchesters f?ngt die volle Atmosph?re eines einzigartigen musikalischen Anlasses ein. Das stellt den Komponisten Felix Mendelssohn in den Mittelpunkt, der 1743 das Gewandhausorchester gr?ndete. Es beinhaltet eine ?berw?ltigende Auff?hrung von Mendelssohns Symphonie Nr. 2, Lobgesang mit seinem feierlichen choralen letzten Satz, sowie die beliebte Ouvert?re aus "Ein Sommernachtstraum" mit hervorragendem Gesangssolisten wie Anne Schwanewilms und Peter Seiffert. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Schumann ? Fantasie in C-Dur: Op. 17
channel.desc: Nachdem er alle 32 Ludwig van Beethoven Klaviersonaten aufgenommen hat, um den 250. Geburtstag des Komponisten zu feiern, entschied sich der gefeierte italienische Pianist Riccardo Schwartz dazu, Soloklavierwerke von Robert Schumann aufzunehmen. Schumanns Fantasie in C, Op. 17, entstand 1836 und wurde vor der Ver?ffentlichung 1839 ?berarbeitet. Sie ist Franz Liszt gewidmet und z?hlt zu den bedeutendsten Klavierwerken Schumanns und der fr?hen Romantik. Die Komposition folgt einer freien Sonatenform: Der erste Satz ist rhapsodisch und leidenschaftlich, der mittlere ein gro?artiges Rondo und das Finale langsam und meditativ. Riccardo Schwartz (1986) hatte das Privileg, als Solist mit vielen weltbekannten Dirigenten, darunter Gustav Kuhn und Yuri Temirkanov, aufzutreten. Er gab gefeierte Klavierrezitals und -konzerte in vielen renommierten hallen. Mit dabei: Riccardo Schwartz.

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Uwe Scholz, einer der bedeutendsten Choreographen des 20. Jahrhunderts, schuf zwei Interpretationen von Igor Strawinskys Le Sacre du Printemps f?r das Leipziger . Sacre I, f?r einen T?nzer, kann als ein d?sterer und bedr?ckender Tanz ?ber Scholzs eigenes Leben interpretiert werden. Dieses einzigartige Solo wird von Giovanni Di Palma zur vierh?ndigen Klavierversion gespielt. channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Kann es uns gelingen, uns in Beethovens kreativen Geist hineinzuversetzen, besonders in der letzten Phase seines Lebens, als er mit schwerem H?rverlust zu k?mpfen hatte? Tom Beghins neue Aufnahme von Beethovens Klaviersonaten Opus 109, 110 und 111 ist eine k?nstlerische Untersuchung dessen, inwiefern Beethovens Musik durch sein direktes Umfeld gepr?gt wurde, das er sich gemeinsam mit der Hilfe von Kollegen und Freunden schuf. Der Pianist Tom Beghin interpretiert hier nicht nur Beethovens Trilogie pianistischer Meisterwerke auf einem gro?artigen neuen Replikat Beethovens Broadwood-Klavieres, sondern verwendet dabei auch eine Rekonstruktion der Geh?rmaschine, die auf dem Klavier des Komponisten montiert war, damit er weiterhin Musik komponieren und spielen konnte, trotz des schwindenden Geh?rsinns. "Sie h?ren besser, wenn Sie Ihren Kopf unter diese Maschine halten, nicht wahr?", fragte Andr? Stein einst Beethoven. Beghin zieht uns in das H?rger?t hinein, wo wir die Essenz von Beethovens wilden und unwiderstehlich poetischen musikalischen Eingebungen f?hlen und h?ren. "Inside the Hearing Machine" l?dt uns auf den multisensorischen Spielplatz eines geh?rlosen Komponisten ein, f?r den die Maschine mehr als ein H?rger?t war und der ?ber viel mehr als nur Klang mit seinem Instrument interagierte. In dieser Auff?hrung f?hrt Les Dissonances die Symphonie Nr. 4 in f-Moll, Op. 36 von Pjotr Iljitsch Tschaikowski auf. Der Komponist schrieb die Symphonie zwischen 1877 und 1878 und widmete sie Nadezhda von Meck ? einer au?erordentlich reichen Witwe und gro?en Bewunderin der Musik Tschaikowskis, die der Komponist als "meine beste Freundin" bezeichnete. Der Komponist erkl?rte in seinen Briefen, dass die Symphonie eine Charakterisierung des Schicksals ist. Das Werk beginnt mit einem kraftvollen Motiv in den H?rnern und Fagotten, das das Schicksal repr?sentiert. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Beethoven ? 1. Klavierkonzert: op. 15
channel.desc: Confusing as it may be: Ludwig van Beethoven's Second Piano Concerto was in fact composed ten years prior to his First Piano Concerto. The cause of this mess lies with the composer himself: Beethoven held back the publication of what we know as the Second Piano Concerto until after that of the First Piano Concerto, so he could thoroughly review the piece. Together with his septet and First Symphony, this piano concerto was finally performed at his official Vienna debut on April 2, 1800 at the Hofburg theatre, with Beethoven himself at the piano. The composer had long ceased to be an unknown in Austria's capital: he had been playing private concerts all around town for years.

Quatuor ?b?ne erforschte jede Facette von Beethovens Streichquartettrepertoire: von den fr?hen Streichquartetten Opus 18 bis zu den Razumovsky-, Harfen- und Serioso-Quartetten (Opus 59, 74 und 95) aus seiner mittleren Schaffensphase und schlie?lich die Tiefe seiner sp?ten Quartette (Opus 127 bis 135). channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Der Maggio Musicale Fiorentino (Florentiner Musikmai) ist das ?lteste Opern- und Musikfestival Italiens. Es wurde 1933 gegr?ndet, urspr?nglich mit dem Ziel, zeitgen?ssische und vergessene Opern zu pr?sentieren. Im Laufe der Jahre hat sich das Spektrum jedoch erheblich erweitert, und Orchesterkonzerte sind l?ngst ein fester Bestandteil des Festivals. Im Rahmen der Ausgabe 2021, dirigiert Maestro Daniel Harding das Orchestra del Maggio Musicale Fiorentino in einem wunderbaren programm mit der Tragischen Ouvert?re in d-Moll, Op. 81 von Johannes Brahms und der Sinfonie Nr. 1 in D-Dur, "Titan" von Gustav Mahler. Brahms komponierte seine ouvert?re im Sommer 1880. Mit ihrem d?steren und st?rmischen Charakter k?nnte sie als ernstes Gegenst?ck zu seiner freudigeren Akademischen Festouvert?re, Op. 80, betrachtet werden. Mahler vollendete seine erste Sinfonie acht Jahre sp?ter. channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Der Schweizer Dirigent Philippe Jordan und das Orchestre de l'Op?ra national de Paris nahmen den kompletten Zyklus der Symphonien von Ludwig van Beethoven in den Jahren 2014-2015 auf. In dieser Auff?hrung dirigiert Jordan Beethovens Symphonie Nr. 1 in C-Dur, Op. 21. Die Symphonie zeigt Beethovens Treue zum Modell der sp?ten Symphonien von Joseph Haydn und Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, aber auch seinen Versuch, sich von seinen Vorg?ngern abzuheben. So beginnt das Werk beispielsweise mit einer langsamen Einleitung, die die Tonart des St?ckes nicht festlegt, was den Zuh?rer verwirrt. Bemerkenswert ist auch die ungew?hnlich hervorgehobene Rolle der Holzbl?ser und der dritte Satz, der als Menuett bezeichnet wird, aber eher den Charakter eines Scherzos hat. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2014 in der Op?ra Bastille in Paris, Frankreich, aufgenommen.

Dar?ber hinaus spielt das Orchester auf historischen Instrumenten, um den Klang von Donizettis Orchester zu rekonstruieren. Zu den Solisten geh?ren Caterina Sala (Adina), Javier Camarena (Nemorino), Florian Sempey (Belcore), Roberto Frontali (Dulcamara), Ana?s Mej?as (Giannetta) und Manuel Ferreira (Zeremonienmeister). Die zwei Werke, die Barati und Debargue spielen, entstanden nur wenige Jahre nacheinander: Brahms 1. Violinsonate ist von 1879 und Francks Sonate in A von 1886. Kristof Barati hatte vor einigen Jahren sogar Brahms Komposition im Studio aufgenommen, und Brahms Sonate z?hlt zu den Favoriten Lucas Debargues. Die zyklische Form und vielen echoartigen Elemente der Klavier- und Violin-Parts vereinen die beiden K?nstler, wie Komplizen, die ihre besten Eigenschaften verschmelzen lassen, um das Beste aus diesen romantischen Werken herauszuholen. channel.desc: Roberto Abbado dirigiert die Filarmonica Arturo Toscanini, den Coro del Teatro Regio di Parma und vier Gesangssolisten in einer herausragenden Auff?hrung von Giuseppe Verdis Messa da Requiem, aufgezeichnet im Parco Ducale di Parma in Italien w?hrend des Festival Verdi 2020. Die Solisten sind Sopranistin Eleonora Buratto, Mezzosopranistin Anita Rachvelishvili, Tenor Giorgio Berrugi und Bass Roberto Tagliavini. Als 1868 sein Komponistenkollege Gioachino Rossini starb, schlug Verdi vor, eine "Messa per Rossini" zu dessen Ehren zu komponieren, die von ihm selbst und mehreren anderen italienischen Komponisten geschrieben werden sollte. Verdi schrieb den abschlie?enden Satz, "Libera me". Als die Premiere abgesagt wurde, wurde das Projekt auf Eis gelegt. Als einige Jahre sp?ter der italienische Dichter Alessandro Manzoni verstarb, nahm Verdi seinen Plan wieder auf, ein Requiem zu komponieren ? diesmal zu Ehren des Dichters, den er so sehr bewunderte. Als Opernkomponist wusste Verdi besser als jeder andere, wie man das Werk dramatisch gestaltet, was in der ?berarbeiteten Version seines "Libera me" deutlich wird. Besonders herausragend ist das ber?hmte, kraftvolle "Dies Irae", das die Schrecken des J?ngsten Gerichts darstellt. Das Athener markierte eine doppelte Premiere: Es war das erste Europakonzert unter der Leitung des neuen Chefdirigenten, sowie das erste Mal, dass Rattle und Barenboim zusammen auftraten. Der Odeon von Herodes Atticus, ein Amphitheater, das 161 nach Christus in Erinnerung an die Frau Herodes Atticus' gebaut wurde, liegt am Hang der Akropolis. Mit einer Sitzkapazit?t von mindestens 5.000 Zuschauern wurde es als das beste Theater in ganz Griechenland betrachtet. Mit dabei: Daniel Barenboim (Klavier).

In dieser spannenden mentation, blicken wir hinter die Kulissen des Opernhauses Z?richs und folgen der intensiven Entwicklung der neuen Produktion von Gioachino Rossinis "Il Barbiere di Siviglia" mit Vesselina Kasarova in der Rolle von Rosina. Der Film zeigt au?erdem die Vorbereitungen f?r andere Produktionen, wie beispielsweise eines Workshops f?r Richard Wagners "Siegfried" inszeniert von Robert Wilson und einer Probe von Igor Strawinskys "Le Sacre du Printemps" mit der Choreografie von Heinz Spoerli. channel.title: CMIM Piano 2024 ? Halbfinale I
channel.desc: Pianist Derek Wang (USA, 1998) tritt mit dem CMIM-Ensemble auf, das aus drei f?hrenden Streichern des Orchestre symphonique de Montr?al besteht. Gemeinsam interpretieren sie den ersten Satz, Allegro, aus Johannes Brahms' Klavierquartett Nr. 1 in g-Moll, Op. 25. Diese Darstellung fand w?hrend der Kammermusikrunde des zweigeteilten Halbfinales der Piano Edition des Concours musical international de Montr?al 2024 (CMIM) statt. Die Aufnahme fand in der Bourgie Hall des Montreal Museum of Fine Arts statt. Mit dabei: Derek Wang (Pianist).

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Berlioz ? Symphonie fantastique: Op. 14
channel.desc: Unter der Leitung von Dirigent Eduard Topchjan f?hrt das Armenische Nationalphilharmonische Orchester Hector Berlioz' Symphonie fantastique, Op. 14 auf. Berlioz komponierte dieses St?ck der Programmmusik im Jahr 1830, als er noch ein Konservatoriumsstudent war. Inspiriert von der unerwiderten Liebe des Komponisten zur irischen Schauspielerin Harriet Smithson, stellt das f?nfs?tzige St?ck die Tr?ume eines jungen K?nstlers dar, der nach einer gescheiterten Liebesaff?re eine ?berdosis Opium genommen hat. Berlioz verwendete in jedem Satz des Werkes eine Melodie, die die Geliebte des K?nstlers darstellt, eine "id?e fixe" (fixe Idee oder Besessenheit). Das Werk ist f?r ein gro?es Orchester geschrieben und bietet eine erstaunliche Palette von Instrumentalfarben, darunter Kirchenglocken, eine Oboe, die abseits der B?hne spielt, und Streicher, die mit dem Holz ihres Bogens spielen (col legno). Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2021 in der Aram Khachaturian halle in Jerewan, Armenien, aufgezeichnet.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: Burgers, beer and barbecue are staples of many adult Americans' diets and the centerpiece of this series hosted by chef and restaurateur Michael Symon; throughout the first season, he heads to three cities across the U.S. -- New York, Nashville and his native Cleveland -- to discover the best each city has to offer in each of the three delicacies featured in the show -- from a Nashville burger joint that creates custom dishes at diners' requests to an over-the-top barbecue joint in the Big Apple; Symon seeks out some hidden -- and not-so-hidden -- gems in the cities he frequents; some of his fellow Food Network personalities, including Bobby Flay and Alex Guarnaschelli, join Symon during his journeys. After Season 1, Symon broadens his scope, expanding his itinerary to add locations in more cities, including New Orleans, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Austin, Texas.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: There's lots to do at a carnival: playing the games, riding the rides, delighting in the noise and the neon. But for some, the best part of a carnival is the food, some of it unique to that milieu. Carnival Eats targets the culinary creations linked to American fairgrounds. Calorie-loaded offerings include rattlesnake, frog legs, or okra -- all deep-fried -- and a decadent sundae of eight doughnuts topped with whipped cream, chocolate or caramel, and don't forget the cherry! Host Noah Cappe, a novice cook, tries his hand at making some of the items.

channel.title: Halloween Baking Championship

The best keep moving through rounds as the tasks and challenges become more complicated. channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Cheap Eats
channel.desc: Traveling can be expensive, with airfare and hotel accommodations often costing hundreds of dollars each, so when you're on a vacation, you likely want to try to cut expenses in some areas. Food blogger Ali Khan can help you save on food costs in various American cities. In each episode of "Cheap Eats," he spends 12 hours in a given locale and has a $35 food budget. With that cash, he must maximize his investment for breakfast, lunch, a snack and dinner -- getting the biggest and tastiest delicacies he can find while staying under his limit. As he explores affordable options in each city, Khan meets with local chefs to find out about the area's culinary scene.

channel.title: Man's Greatest Food
channel.desc: No eatery is too far for Roger Mooking, as he sets out on a culinary pilgrimage to find the greatest foods. He works to visit the 15 best spots for America's most beloved and succulent foods, including mouth-watering steaks and smoky barbecue, seafood from the Pacific to the Atlantic and down to the bayou, sandwiches, pork, large pizzas, and a favorite of American households, juicy hamburgers. Mooking visits locations such as Louisiana and Florida and travels from Miami to New Orleans.

channel.title: Man Fire Food
channel.desc: Roger Mooking has a fascination with fire. The chef enjoys finding inventive ways to cook with fire, which is exactly what he does in this series that takes him on a journey across the U.S. He visits pit-masters, chefs and home cooks who use fire to create complex, flavorful dishes. The people Mooking visits don't simply turn on a stove and start cooking; their methods include cooking over an open fire in a rustic chuck wagon and smoking meats in a former airplane that a mechanic has transformed into a smoker.

channel.title: Man Fire Food
channel.desc: Roger Mooking has a fascination with fire. The chef enjoys finding inventive ways to cook with fire, which is exactly what he does in this series that takes him on a journey across the U.S. He visits pit-masters, chefs and home cooks who use fire to create complex, flavorful dishes. The people Mooking visits don't simply turn on a stove and start cooking; their methods include cooking over an open fire in a rustic chuck wagon and smoking meats in a former airplane that a mechanic has transformed into a smoker.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Food Paradise
channel.desc: There is, of course, much more to a vacation experience than hotels, sightseeing and souvenirs. For a look at what is literally on the menu, Travel Channel takes a tour of the must-see eateries across the country where a one-of-a-kind dining experience can be had. There are places that serve lip-smacking pizza, tasty deli entrees, boatloads of bacon, fresh seafood, finger-licking deep-fried dishes, juicy steaks, hot-and-spicy favorites -- the list that can whet anyone's appetite goes on and on. Each episode focuses on a specific type of food, and there's even episodic room reserved for desserts, such as ice cream and pie.

channel.title: Iron Chef America
channel.desc: Based upon the format of the original Japanese version of "Iron Chef," the series features a Kitchen Stadium filled with culinary equipment. At the beginning of the episode, an outside challenger chooses one of Kitchen Stadium's resident chefs to compete against. Then the host unveils a "secret ingredient," which the competing chefs must incorporate into each dish they create.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: The Best Thing I Ever Ate
channel.desc: A look at what celebrity chefs and Food Network hosts like to eat when the cameras stop rolling. Each episode of the series will delve into some of the network stars' favorite food spots and the meals that they would travel thousands of miles to have again. They dish on fantastic desserts, the best barbecue joints and where to find the comfort foods they crave. Each bite is a trip down memory lane as they recount stories of healing and discovery through their most cherished treats and eats.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods America
channel.desc: The continuation of "Bizarre Foods" finds Andrew Zimmern keeping his passport at home, as the chef and writer embarks on a culinary exploration of the great U, S of A. From traditional foods passed down through generations to modern eats whose roots are purely American, the United States is home to a smorgasbord of bizarre foods and equally extraordinary stories associated with them. So who best to taste and tell than Andrew, the man who lives by the motto "If it looks good, eat it"? The cultural cuisine master has done plenty of that throughout the history of "Bizarre Foods," with the "America" incarnation including a celebration of the series' 100th episode.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods: Delicious Destinations
channel.desc: Andrew Zimmern's culinary curiosity knows no bounds. Extending his popular "Bizarre Foods" franchise, the James Beard Award-winning chef continues his quest to find the most interesting dishes around the world. From melt-in-your-mouth chocolate in Zurich to decadent gelato in Florence, savory paella in Barcelona to creamy clam chowder in Boston, Zimmern samples quintessential, "to die for" delicacies that define iconic cities. Each half-hour episode focuses on one destination's classic foods -- where they came from, how they are prepared, and the right way to eat them.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Man v. Food
channel.desc: In one of the most popular series in Travel Channel's history, actor Casey Webb -- assuming the mantle from original host Adam Richman -- travels across America to sample some iconic regional dishes and take on some daunting food challenges, such as attacking a pitcher-sized bloody mary garnished with a whole fried chicken, tucking into a four-and-a-half-pound Reuben sandwich, and a choice between taking on a 151-ounce milkshake, an eight-pound sloppy joe or eating six habanero ghost chili wings. Talk about the big, the bad or the burn!

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: There's lots to do at a carnival: playing the games, riding the rides, delighting in the noise and the neon. But for some, the best part of a carnival is the food, some of it unique to that milieu. Carnival Eats targets the culinary creations linked to American fairgrounds. Calorie-loaded offerings include rattlesnake, frog legs, or okra -- all deep-fried -- and a decadent sundae of eight doughnuts topped with whipped cream, chocolate or caramel, and don't forget the cherry! Host Noah Cappe, a novice cook, tries his hand at making some of the items.

channel.desc: In one of the most popular series in Travel Channel's history, actor Casey Webb -- assuming the mantle from original host Adam Richman -- travels across America to sample some iconic regional dishes and take on some daunting food challenges, such as attacking a pitcher-sized bloody mary garnished with a whole fried chicken, tucking into a four-and-a-half-pound Reuben sandwich, and a choice between taking on a 151-ounce milkshake, an eight-pound sloppy joe or eating six habanero ghost chili wings. Talk about the big, the bad or the burn!

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: There's lots to do at a carnival: playing the games, riding the rides, delighting in the noise and the neon. But for some, the best part of a carnival is the food, some of it unique to that milieu. Carnival Eats targets the culinary creations linked to American fairgrounds. Calorie-loaded offerings include rattlesnake, frog legs, or okra -- all deep-fried -- and a decadent sundae of eight doughnuts topped with whipped cream, chocolate or caramel, and don't forget the cherry! Host Noah Cappe, a novice cook, tries his hand at making some of the items.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: Burgers, beer and barbecue are staples of many adult Americans' diets and the centerpiece of this series hosted by chef and restaurateur Michael Symon; throughout the first season, he heads to three cities across the U.S. -- New York, Nashville and his native Cleveland -- to discover the best each city has to offer in each of the three delicacies featured in the show -- from a Nashville burger joint that creates custom dishes at diners' requests to an over-the-top barbecue joint in the Big Apple; Symon seeks out some hidden -- and not-so-hidden -- gems in the cities he frequents; some of his fellow Food Network personalities, including Bobby Flay and Alex Guarnaschelli, join Symon during his journeys. After Season 1, Symon broadens his scope, expanding his itinerary to add locations in more cities, including New Orleans, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Austin, Texas.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Good Eats
channel.desc: Equal parts smart and sardonic, creator and host Alton Brown uses a combination of classroom methods and wacky comedy sketches to explain not just how to whip up an excellent dish, but also why the ingredients interact as they do when you put them all together. Brown has said that the show's inspiration is to combine Julia Child, Mr. Wizard and "Monty Python."

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods: Delicious Destinations
channel.desc: Andrew Zimmern's culinary curiosity knows no bounds. Extending his popular "Bizarre Foods" franchise, the James Beard Award-winning chef continues his quest to find the most interesting dishes around the world. From melt-in-your-mouth chocolate in Zurich to decadent gelato in Florence, savory paella in Barcelona to creamy clam chowder in Boston, Zimmern samples quintessential, "to die for" delicacies that define iconic cities. Each half-hour episode focuses on one destination's classic foods -- where they came from, how they are prepared, and the right way to eat them.

channel.desc: Families share how their questions have been answered not by blind faith, but through walking by faith.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Mother Angelica Live Classics
channel.desc: Mother looks to the Scriptures and talks about how rash judgments we make lead us away from God. But He is always willing to forgive us when we turn back to him.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Real Life Catholic
channel.desc: Chris Stefanick and survivalist Will Hince journey through the wilderness.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Lent
channel.desc: The Samaritan woman at the well met Jesus and experienced illumination.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Life on the rock
channel.desc: Br. Mark continues his conversation with Marcel LeJeune, President and Founder of Catholic Missionary Disciples, about the importance of parish renewal and evangelization.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: The Faithful Traveler In Portugal
channel.desc: Journey to Cais da Ribeira for a meal and tour the Ferriera Port Wine House.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: EWTN Vaticano
channel.desc: Latest news from the Vatican with excerpts and analysis of the Holy Fathers recent audiences and writings, and other featured segments.[(96057)]

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: My Lourdes Faith Journey
channel.desc: Pilgrimage volunteer Alley Marrow recounts how her Lourdes experience has helped her heal from the anger she suffered because of sexual molestation, the loss of a parent, and the loss of a child during pregnancy. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: World Over
channel.desc: Each week, Raymond Arroyo challenges viewers with important political and cultural reporting and analysis of a wide variety of topics of interest to Catholics and people of faith. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Ewtn Pro Life Weekly
channel.desc: EWTN Pro-Life Weekly is a half-hour news and commentary program that covers life issues including abortion, assisted suicide, in vitro fertilization, highlighting the mercy of a culture of life, from a Catholic perspective. This program features interviews, analysis, and actionable steps for viewers to defend the dignity of every human person from conception to natural death. Hosted by Abigail Galv?n. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Real Life Catholic
channel.desc: In the Northwest, Chris Stefanick meets Catholic families who are passionate about winemaking, beer crafting, and their faith. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: At Home With Jim And Joy
channel.desc: Author and founder of Chastity Project and JP2 Trails, Jason Evert is back with Jim and Joy to speak about gender in today?s world and how to respond with charity and clarity. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Lord, Have Mercy
channel.desc: Mike Aquilina and Dr. Scott Hahn discuss Scott's book, Lord, Have Mercy: The Healing Power of Confession. They talk about why Confession is referred to as "the Sacrament of Healing". (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: new! Ewtn News Nightly
channel.desc: EWTN News Nightly is our daily news and analysis program presenting breaking Catholic News worldwide, top stories, and daily reports from the White House, Capitol Hill, and Rome. Weekdays at 6 & 9 PM EST. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Priests And Deacons: Ministers Of Mercy
channel.desc: Deacon Harold Burke-Sivers and Fr. Brian Mullady examine the necessity of not just waiting for people to come to the priests and deacons, but of going out to them as Jesus did. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Franciscan University Presents
channel.desc: Fr. Gregory Pine, OP, shares how we can use speech for the Kingdom and push out the sins of speech, specifically during the season of Lent in order to better train our tongues. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: new! Ewtn News In Depth
channel.desc: EWTN?s weekly one-hour discussion of current events in the Church, politics, and culture, from a Catholic perspective. Covering the underreported stories and clarifying the Church's position on key teachings, with a focus on the laity's needs and concerns. Hosted by Catherine Hadro. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Africa Life Under Siege
channel.desc: At a recent international pro-life conference, bishops, priests and other concerned individuals discussed the serious issues that are drastically influencing African culture, including pressure from the West to give up their pro-life attitudes and culture. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Ewtn News Nightly
channel.desc: EWTN News Nightly is our daily news and analysis program presenting breaking Catholic News worldwide, top stories, and daily reports from the White House, Capitol Hill, and Rome. Weekdays at 6 & 9 PM EST. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Daily Mass
channel.desc: The Franciscan Missionaries of the Eternal Word celebrate Mass from the Our Lady of Angels Chapel in Irondale, AL. (LIVE DAILY at 8 am Eastern). (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Holy Land Rosary
channel.desc: Fr. Mitch Pacwa leads the Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary from the actual holy sites and shrines where they took place, bringing the Gospels to life and offering a deeper understanding of the Rosary meditations. (19 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Litany Of The Blessed Virgin Mary
channel.desc: Join the Franciscan Missionaries of the Eternal Word as they recite this beautiful prayer in honor of the Blessed Virgin Mary from the Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament in Hanceville, Alabama. (11 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Fulton J. Sheen: A Voice That Was Raised
channel.desc: Fr. Andrew Apostoli discusses Archbishop Sheen's love of the Blessed Sacrament and Adoration. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Father Spitzer?s Universe
channel.desc: Fr. Spitzer answers viewer questions on a wide range of subjects, including: Reason, Faith, Suffering, Virtue, and the Existence of God. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Women Of Grace
channel.desc: Jesse Romero discusses his encounters with the diabolical while serving as a sheriff in Los Angeles. Hosted by Johnnette Williams, part 3 of 3. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Lent At Ephesus
channel.desc: The Benedictines of Mary, Queen of Apostles in Northwest Missouri transform their priory into a modern, high-tech recording studio for three days to produce an album of sacred music for the Lenten season. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Stones And Pearls: The Rosary In The Holy Land
channel.desc: The first glorious mystery takes us to the tomb of Christ. Here in a cave in Jerusalem, the grave lies empty and pilgrims can see what the apostles did, that through God we will conquer death and experience eternal life. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Friar
channel.desc: After the local bakery reports that several boxes of cookies have gone missing, Leopoldo the frog worries that the cookies gifted to them by a friend were the ones stolen from there. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The First Saturdays For Kids
channel.desc: Sister Lucia teaches four children the importance of the First Saturday devotion, and the four steps necessary for fulfilling her request in this animated special. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Icons
channel.desc: The special needs children discover the power of persistence on their pilgrimage to the site of the Virgin Mary?s miraculous apparitions at Lourdes. Through faith and prayer, they learn that all things are possible. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Chaplet Of St. Michael
channel.desc: Mother Angelica and the Nuns of Our Lady of the Angels Monastery ask for the intercession of the Prince of the Heavenly Hosts and the nine Choirs of Angels, as they pray the chaplet of St. Michael. (30 minutes).[(96057)]

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Magical Japanese
channel.desc: The Japanese language is rich in words and expressions influenced by nature, history and culture. This episode introduces words associated with water. Water has long been regarded as plentiful and accessible in Japan. It is deeply embedded in Japanese culture and is even used to describe human relationships and life itself. Poet, literary translator and long-time Japan resident Peter MacMillan guides us through these unique words and the culture behind them.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: The Onabare festival is a 300-year-old folk cultural property in Kami, Kochi Prefecture. A portable shrine is paraded through the streets, with dancing and other performances taking place along the way. The highlight is nerikomi, which involves the careful wielding of a long, heavy pole. We see a first-timer and others battling through a tough training process, as they prepare to attempt a remarkable feat of skill and strength that is a key feature of this local matsuri tradition.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Tiny Desk Concerts Japan
channel.desc: \"New\" Traditional Japanese Music: Piano, Shamisen, and Electronic Sounds\nSince debuting with her 1976 album JAPANESE GIRL, Yano Akiko has been a trailblazer in blending Japanese culture with her unique musical style, including collaborations with Yellow Magic Orchestra. Agatsuma Hiromitsu, a renowned shamisen virtuoso, has been redefining \"tradition and innovation\" through performances that transcend genres and borders. The two artists come together for yano et agatsuma and take on tiny desk concerts JAPAN! Joined by Fukasawa Hideyuki on synthesizer, the trio introduces the world to a new type of Japanese music rooted in folk traditions and classic melodies.

channel.desc: Kata-yuzen is a Kyoto yuzen dyeing method that sometimes requires as many as 100 stencils to complete a bolt of kimono fabric. channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Seasoning The Seasons
channel.desc: The calmness of Seto Inland Sea, located in western Japan, will send your worries away. One thing that has been firmly supporting lives in this area is stone. The stone walls of the famous Osaka Castle are made of one million pieces of stone, most of which were granite quarried from the islands in the Seto Inland Sea, and shipped to parts of Japan. In this episode, we travel to the coastal area of the Seto Inland Sea, where life involves around reliable yet warm stones.

channel.desc: Find the best in health and fitness products to give you a spring in your step and a healthier lifestyle. From top tips and great gadgets, we'll help you to revitalise your daily routine.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: 1PM with Izabel London
channel.desc: Elevate your style with Izabel London. Discover chic, versatile fashion pieces to refresh your wardrobe, all at 1PM.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Garden Solutions with Block Blitz
channel.desc: Transform your outdoor space with Garden Solutions featuring Block Blitz. Discover easy, effective ways to clean and protect patios, paths, and driveways.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Elemis Skin Therapies
channel.desc: Care for your mind and body holistically and sensuously with therapeutic aromatherapy. Elemis are famed for their premier spa and salon treatments, and for the absolute purity of their plant oils.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Skechers Footwear
channel.desc: Step out in style in Skechers! Renowned for their on-trend, sporty designs, you can now find their fab shoes at QVC too.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: New Season Izabel London Fashion
channel.desc: Enliven your wardrobe with Izabel London's new season of style, offering gorgeous fashion in inclusive sizing. Feel fabulous every day with this cutting-edge collection.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Tili Beauty
channel.desc: Effortlessly update your daily beauty routine with Tili, from beauty tools and everyday essentials, to expert developed fitness and wellbeing items, we've got you covered. Try it, love it with Tili.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Denim & Co
channel.desc: Join us to see Denim & Co's clothing range offering trend-focused pieces combined with timeless style and chic choices for your smart or casual looks.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Elemis Skin Therapies
channel.desc: Care for your mind and body holistically and sensuously with therapeutic aromatherapy. Elemis are famed for their premier spa and salon treatments, and for the absolute purity of their plant oils.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Lara Pearls Collection
channel.desc: Harness the beauty of pearls with the Lara Pearls Collection, offering stunning jewellery set with elegant pearls for over 20 years. Discover a piece for your jewellery box or a loved one's today.

channel.name: QVC UK
channel.title: Skechers Footwear
channel.desc: Step out in style in Skechers! Renowned for their on-trend, sporty designs, you can now find their fab shoes at QVC too.[(96057)]
